iconicAnchor.label: Brutalist-informed heavy type and architectural grid systems
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Contemporary graphic designers adapting Brutalist mass and structure
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: AIGA's design publication documents severely gridded, condensed, rough-edged typography that translates Brutalist weight and material directness into graphic form.

sources.title: A Severely Gridded, Heavy-as-Cement Font That's A Little Rough Around the Edges
supports: Brutalist influence can be translated through harsh geometry, condensed weight, severe grids, and rough character.
Large-scale display type can operate as a dense shape while a lighter text face preserves reading.

sources.title: If Graphic Design and Architecture Had a Baby It'd Look Like Main Studio's Latest Identity
supports: A modular grid derived from Brutalist architecture can organize a repeatable identity across many outputs.
Monospaced type and rough Risograph texture show how structure and production surface can work together.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches typographic, high contrast, raw form, edge defined, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/graphic-brutalism/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
